body.statement: If a probability law on \(\mathbb R\) has finite moments \(m_k\) of all orders and \(\sum_{s=1}^{\infty}m_{2s}^{-1/(2s)}=\infty\), then the law is determined by its moment sequence.

source.locator: Chapter I, Carleman's criterion for the Hamburger moment problem
source.verbatim_statement: If the sum from n=1 to infinity of m_(2n)^(-1/(2n)) diverges, the Hamburger moment problem is determinate.

attestation.note: Verified against the searchable lawful scan of Shohat–Tamarkin, The Problem of Moments, AMS Mathematical Surveys vol. 1, Chapter I, and the AMS-linked bibliographic record on 2026-09-05.
